title: Shakira Sets Amazon Music Livestream Record With Madrid Show and Dua Lipa Duet
excerpt: Shakira's October 3 Madrid concert became Amazon Music's most-viewed livestream by a female artist, with Dua Lipa joining her as a surprise guest.
body:
Shakira's October 3 Madrid concert became Amazon Music's most-viewed livestream by a female artist, with Dua Lipa joining her as a surprise guest. They performed "Antología," and Amazon announced the record the following day without releasing a viewer total. The concert streamed worldwide through Amazon Music, Prime Video and Twitch, making it Shakira's first full-concert global livestream. No paid subscription was required, and a 24-hour replay followed the live broadcast. Before the show, Shakira said she was excited to take the tour further by sharing the Madrid night with fans around the world.

Dua Lipa joined Shakira for "Antología," the ballad from *Pies Descalzos*, released in 1995. The Madrid appearance was their first performance together, either onstage or in a studio. Organizers considered two songs for the guest spot and ultimately chose "Antología" for the duet. The decision also carried some history of its own. During her 2025 stop in Bogotá, Dua Lipa covered the song as part of the local-song tradition she used throughout the *Radical Optimism Tour*. Shakira later praised that performance online. The Madrid version therefore connected that earlier cover with Shakira's original catalog nearly three decades later.

The livestream came from Shakira Stadium, a temporary venue built inside Madrid's Iberdrola Music complex for the residency. It holds more than 50,000 people and was designed by Bjarke Ingels Group, the architecture studio behind the temporary venue used for Adele's 2024 residency in Munich. The scale makes the Madrid run different from a conventional arena stop, but the stadium is only one part of the project.

The residency also marks Shakira's first concerts in Spain in eight years. What began as a three-night return expanded repeatedly as demand grew. The Madrid run now serves as the European closing chapter of the *Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour*.

Around the stadium, ES LATINA extends the residency into Macondo Park, a temporary cultural site curated around Latin music and culture. Its eight spaces include a museum devoted to Shakira's career, a literature area inspired by Gabriel García Márquez, workshops, food and fashion programming, and a second music stage. One of those spaces, La Sala, hosts a secondary stage before the main concert with alternative artists selected from Shakira's favorites. Access to Macondo Park is tied to a Shakira concert ticket, so it functions as part of the residency rather than as a separate festival elsewhere in Madrid.

The October 3 stream carried that larger Madrid setup to viewers outside the venue for one night. For a show built around Shakira's current era, its biggest surprise reached back three decades. "Antología" became the first song Shakira and Dua Lipa had ever performed together.
